clue.text: Bean plant chopper chopped British one

indicators.note: a chopped word has been cut short, so the last letter of the tool comes off

parts.note: an adze is a chopping tool for shaping timber
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool has hacked down a bean plant belonging to a Briton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' trims ADZE to ADZ before UK and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The adzuki is a leguminous plant grown in East Asia for its small red edible seeds.

clue.text: Hard to forget duck by poor player in university

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the zero-shaped duck is dropped from the stern word

parts.note: dour means hard, stern or severe
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: A tough cricketer at a university is slow to get over scoring nothing next to a weak teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forget' takes O out of DOUR, leaving DUR, and HAM goes beside it ('by').
explanation.definitionFit: Durham is the home of an ancient English university, the third oldest in England.

clue.text: Undoing engineering union holding strike leads to no good

indicators.note: holding means the reworked union letters keep the blow inside them
engineering means contriving or rearranging, so the letters of union are reorganised

parts.note: to butt is to strike with the head

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An engineers' union's strike leads nowhere good, undoing its cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineering' rearranges UNION as UN...ONI; 'holding' puts BUTT between UN and ONI, and 'leads to' gives NG from 'no good'. 'engineering union' looks like one body, the AEU, but 'engineering' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing a coat means opening its fastenings, which is what unfastening its buttons does.

clue.text: Less clothing needed at first in French island's conditions

indicators.note: in means the whole clothed group goes inside the French islands

parts.note: île is French for island, so ILES, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: clothing means the word less is wrapped round the letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: On a French island you need fewer clothes, for health reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives N from 'needed'; 'clothing' puts it in LESS to make LNESS, and 'in' puts that inside ILES (French islands). Read the 's of 'island's' as the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Illnesses are medical conditions, the sense of conditions as ailments or disorders.

clue.text: James's valet embraces a lady without notice, in sweetly old-fashioned way

indicators.note: embraces means the valet's name wraps round the letter

parts.note: Peter Quint is the dead valet in Henry James's The Turn of the Screw

indicators.note: an ad is a notice, so the lady is written without those two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentleman's gentleman hugs a woman unannounced, in a charmingly antiquated manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without notice' takes AD from LADY, leaving LY. James is Henry James, not a modern employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaintly means in an attractively unusual or old-fashioned manner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Argue toss over equal rights

indicators.note: tossing letters over throws them about, so they are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right, so two rights are R and R

explanation.surface: Argue over flipping a coin for equal rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toss over' mixes EQUAL with RR (two rights).
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel is to argue angrily, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Maeterlinck's heart of gold

indicators.note: the heart of a name is what remains when the first and last letters go

parts.note: the Belgian playwright Maeterlinck's first name was Maurice

explanation.surface: The Belgian playwright had a heart of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' trims M and E from MAURICE, the first name of Maurice Maeterlinck.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric is the adjective for gold, from the Latin aurum.

clue.text: Sister one day rescued from flood

indicators.note: rescued from means these pieces are taken out of the flood word

parts.note: to inundate is to flood
the Roman numeral I is one
a date is a particular day

explanation.surface: A nun and another person were saved from rising floodwater one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescued from' removes I and DATE from INUNDATE, leaving NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order of women, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Note in words of song sound rhyme

indicators.note: sound tells us the result is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the note ME (the tonic sol-fa mi) inside LYRIC, words of a song, gives LYMERIC

explanation.surface: A note within the lyrics of a song produces a good rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: ME, a spelling of the sol-fa note mi, goes 'in' LYRIC (words of song); 'sound' says LYMERIC is only heard, and spelt as the comic verse form.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a humorous five-line poem with an AABBA rhyme scheme, so a rhyme in the sense of verse.

clue.text: Girl thoroughly English, got back on horse

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

indicators.note: got back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: all means wholly or thoroughly, as in all done

explanation.surface: A thoroughly English girl climbed back on her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got back' turns ALL + E into ELLA, which goes after ARAB ('on').
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a girl's name, the type of definition crosswords often use for forenames.

clue.text: Call again before noon, visiting Frenchman

indicators.note: something visiting is inside, so the morning letters go within the French name

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
a.m., ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: Ring back before midday while a Frenchman is staying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' puts AM inside RENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rename something is to give it a new name, to call it again by another title.

clue.text: Keep a piece in the corner

definitions.meaning: a keep is the strongest central tower of a fortified building, by extension the stronghold
the chess rook stands in a corner square of the board at the start

explanation.surface: A rook is guarded in the corner of the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortress, and in chess the rook is also called by that name.

clue.text: Branch specialised in launching carpeting line

parts.note: a carpeting is a severe telling-off, as is a rocket in British slang
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A firm involved in launching new carpeting lines.
explanation.walkthrough: A rocket is British slang for a reprimand, a carpeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the branch of science and engineering dealing with launching rockets.

clue.text: Sparks thrilling Scotsman

parts.note: electric means thrilling or exciting
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scot who sends sparks flying is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparks is a traditional nickname for an electrician; the capital S hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is an old informal nickname for a tradesman who wires buildings.

clue.text: Old boy, only one dropping out of physics perhaps, getting past it

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

indicators.note: dropping out of means this letter leaves the subject word

parts.note: physics is an example of a science
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A former pupil, the only one to drop out of physics, is losing his edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping out of' removes I from SCIENCE, giving SCENCE; 'perhaps' marks physics as just one science.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolescence is the process of becoming outdated or no longer useful, of being past it.

clue.text: Sweet fairy dancing

definitions.meaning: a sweet is a small confection or candy
in Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker ballet the fairy of this name dances a famous solo

explanation.surface: A pretty fairy is performing a ballet solo.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugarplum is a small boiled sweet, and the Nutcracker's dancing fairy shares the name.

clue.text: Highness, take time for second opinion

indicators.note: for second means the second letter is swapped for the new one

parts.note: altitude is height, highness

explanation.surface: Your Highness, take time to get a second opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take time for second': T replaces L, the second letter of ALTITUDE. Highness with its royal capital is really height.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a settled way of thinking about something, an opinion or stance.

clue.text: After early appearance knocks out T-shirt as gift

indicators.note: knocks out suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A T-shirt received as a present stuns its recipient straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks out' jumbles the twelve letters of T-SHIRT AS GIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on first glance, judging after only an early appearance or impression.

clue.text: Do engraving in blue, lacking detail

indicators.note: in means the engraving word sits inside the colour word

parts.note: sky blue, and the sky itself, is blue
to etch is to engrave a design with acid

explanation.surface: An artist working an engraving in blue has left out the fine detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ETCH inside SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sketchy is rough and incomplete, like a quick sketch lacking detail.

clue.text: Stand still holding old assistant up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole is read from bottom to top
holding means the first word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: yet means still, as in yet more
PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A stand-in holds still while an old assistant gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O + PA into YET to give YOPAET, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapoy is a small three-legged table, a kind of stand for a tea service.

clue.text: One requesting bowl for giant cabbage?

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the merry old monarch called for his pipe and his bowl
cole is cabbage, and a king-size one is a giant, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a bowl to hold an enormous cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme monarch called for his bowl, and kale-type cabbage is cole, king-sized.

clue.text: Waste of running water

parts.note: taken as written
the Fal is a river in Cornwall, running water

explanation.surface: Running water should not be wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is waste or refuse, as well as the edible inner parts of a slaughtered animal.

clue.text: Poured wine over in a cocktail

indicators.note: over means the wine is placed round the other letters

parts.note: red is red wine

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Wine was poured over the ice in a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes IN A into AIN, and 'over' puts RED round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rained, in the sense of fell in torrents, means poured down heavily.

clue.text: Block of copper one loaded

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a toff is a rich upper-class person, someone loaded with money

explanation.surface: A block of copper has been loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Toff is British slang for a rich or posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off is to block or isolate, as a supply can be cut off.

clue.text: Middlesbrough holding the ball up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
holding means the town's name contains the letters within it

explanation.surface: Middlesbrough keeps the ball in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' points to BRO inside Middlesbrough, and 'up' turns it round. Middlesbrough is a town in north-east England with a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or globe, so a ball.

clue.text: Name one poet who has scratched head for inspiration

parts.note: to call is to name
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, so the first letter of the poet is crossed off

parts.note: Alexander Pope was an English poet

explanation.surface: Name the poet who scratched his head looking for inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has scratched head' takes P from POPE, leaving OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek muse of epic poetry, a muse being a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Learner bravely struggling with speech

indicators.note: struggling suggests something writhing about, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates
taken as written

explanation.surface: A learner bravely struggles to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges L + BRAVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbally means in spoken words, by means of speech rather than writing.

clue.text: Rogues removed core funds

indicators.note: removing the core takes out the middle letter of the word

parts.note: monkeys are mischievous rascals, as in cheeky monkey

explanation.surface: Thieves removed the core funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed core' takes out K, the middle letter of MONKEYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneys is a plural of money, meaning sums or funds.
